You can find visiting information and book a visit on the Elmley Prison main page.

Our commitment to you

At HMP Elmley, we understand that strong family relationships are essential for helping people turn their lives around.

Staying connected with loved ones not only reduces the risk of reoffending but also promotes stability and emotional wellbeing.

These positive links can lower anxiety, self-harm and depression, creating a safer and more supportive environment for everyone.

Family connections play a key role in rehabilitation and in building a safer, more stable prison community. That’s why we actively listen to feedback from both prisoners and their families.

We’ve scheduled focus groups with prisoners and are gathering input from visitors to help us reflect on what’s working and where we can improve.

This feedback will shape how we deliver family services in the future.

We share the vision set out in the Farmer Review, which calls family ties the ’golden thread‘ running through all prison policy.

Looking ahead, we’ll continue to introduce new initiatives that strengthen these relationships, guided by both local strategies and the Review’s recommendations.

Our commitment is clear; we will keep reviewing and improving our Family Services in partnership with our provider, Prison Advice and Care Trust (PACT), to ensure families remain at the heart of rehabilitation.

The Family Pathway at HMP Elmley is overseen by senior managers, who lead on Reducing Reoffending.

This work is managed through a range of forums and meeting structures to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including:

Senior Leaders Team (SLT)

PACT Performance Meetings

Reducing Reoffending Meeting

Quality Improvement Group

Family Forum - Head of Reducing Reoffending attends the visits centre monthly to speak to families and gain feedback.

In addition, we have a dedicated Family Services Champion, a Custodial Manager within the prison, playing a key role in driving this work forward and ensuring families remain central to our approach.

Support and services offered

Visitors centre

The visitor centre is the first point of contact for many visitors and provides a warm, welcoming environment outside the prison.

It houses the main PACT office, staffed by the Family Support Team, Family Champion Custodial Manager and the visits booking team, who are available to support visitors.

The centre provides information on the visits process, family days, prisoner work opportunities at Elmley, healthcare and wellbeing and key contact details.

Prisoners from nearby HMP Standford Hill, employed on Release on Temporary Licence also welcome visitors and offer practical insight into the services available at Elmley and the experience of serving there.

Children’s play facilities

The centre offers a range of age-appropriate activities for children.

Facilities include a quiet, well-stocked reading corner where families can read together and take books home, toys and games for younger children, a large-screen TV and games consoles for older children.

Child-friendly books also explain the visits process, searches and the role of prison dogs.

Within the visits hall there are books, games, games consoles and a soft-play area, alongside sensory aids to support neurodivergent children.

Our Neurodiversity Support Manager, Security team and PACT work together to break down barriers and to create safe spaces within visits to support visitors with neurodiverse needs.

If you have a family member that requires adjustments in order to be able to attend visits, then please speak to our visits staff.

Foreign national phone credit and letters

Foreign national prisoners are entitled to convert their standard visiting orders into phone credit to make calls abroad or send airmail letters.

In addition to this any prisoner who will not receive any visits is able to apply for pin credit from the Family GP Fund.

Family engagement work

Family Engagement Workers at Elmley support prisoners with family contact and communication.

They provide one-to-one emotional and practical parenting support, helping prisoners maintain family ties, strengthen communication and build positive relationships.

As part of the first night process, they identify concerns early and refer prisoners to other agencies where appropriate.

A Family Engagement Worker based at the local court can also help to identify issues before a prisoner arrives at Elmley.

Secure social video call support

We have video calls available on both Saturday and Sunday mornings.

You can read more about how video calling works here.

Parenting and relationship courses

One-to-one work is provided by PACT on a case by case basis.

Change, Grow, Live chairty also provide support together with our Offender Management Unit.

Family support

Elmley works with a range of partners and agencies to deliver its Families and Significant Others Strategy (FaSO).

Support includes:

one-to-one interventions

family forums in the visits centre with the Head of Reducing Reoffending

group sessions

family engagement and outreach

a Family Engagement worker based at the local courts

A custodial manager serves as Family Champion, promoting the strategy and driving its delivery.

Partners work closely with the Offender Management Unit, key workers and other teams within the prison to ensure all family contact and support meets safeguarding requirements.

PACT is Elmley’s principal family services partner. You can read more about the work of PACT.

Family days

We hold 13 family days each year, including opportunities for wider family members to visit, ensuring everyone can maintain important relationships.

We also offer 2 additional family days for those engaging with Drug and Alcohol services (via Change, Live, Grow charity).

Family days are themed around seasonal occasions, including Christmas, Easter, Valentine’s day and the summer holidays.

Family Days run from 9:30am to 3:30pm.

We provide a free lunch for families and prisoners.

Morning activities include a reading corner, games consoles, face painting, refreshments and staff-led family bonding sessions in the gym.

The afternoon programme features themed entertainment, such as performers and music, and families can have photographs taken with their loved ones.

Library

Family projects that are run by Library staff include:

Storybook: open to any prisoner with young children in the family, so not just Dads! Younger siblings, nieces and nephews can receive stories.

Storybook ’Me and You‘: this is an activity sheet for our prisoners to complete and send out to their young family members

Raising Readers: open to any prisoner with young children and teenagers in the family

Care leavers

We work collaboratively with advisors from the local authority to support those with care experience and feel that we have a good understanding of care leavers needs.

Forums are facilitated by our safety colleagues and outcomes are shared with relevant teams within the prison.

For those in custody that have come from a care experienced background we offer ongoing support via our partners and key worker scheme.

Safeguarding measures

We provide dedicated phone numbers for families to raise any concerns about a loved one in custody - whether related to bullying, violence, self-harm, or other issues.

You can read about reporting concerns on our main page.

Phone numbers are also clearly displayed in the visitor centre and visits hall.

For care leavers, our Offender Management Unit has a dedicated staff member who leads on care leaver support.

They can be contacted through the Safer Custody team for advice and assistance on 01795 880 921.

For further reference to safeguarding measures, please see the HMPPS Child Safeguarding Policy Framework.

What we have achieved

We have taken several important steps to strengthen family ties and address the priorities highlighted in the The Farmer Review

Family-friendly visitor centre: we offer a welcoming environment for families and is staffed by dedicated PACT family workers who offer support and guidance.

Storybook Dads: through our library, all prisoners can record stories to share with their children, helping maintain meaningful connections. We’ve also delivered creative courses where prisoners design and write stories that are published into books - a hugely popular initiative we plan to continue to provide.

Family days: we hold 13 family days each year, including opportunities for wider family members to visit, ensuring everyone can maintain important relationships. We also offer 2 additional family days for those engaging with Drug and Alcohol services (via the Change, Live Grow charity).

Family-Friendly Catering: working with PACT, we’ve introduced themed days around key events and celebrations to make visits more enjoyable.

Fair access to family days: we’ve reviewed our allocation process to ensure all children have the right to spend time with their parents in custody.

Secure video visits: available on application, this helps families to stay connected when in-person visits aren’t possible.

First night support: PACT now plays a key role in our induction process, offering advice and guidance on family contact during what can be a stressful time.

‘You Said, We Did’ feedback: visitors can share their views via feedback forms in the visitor centre. This input informs our Reducing Reoffending strategy, and actions taken will be published for transparency.

Monthly family forum: our Head of reducing reoffending attends the visits centre monthly to talk to families about any issues and to feed back from the previous months meeting.

Monthly prisoner forum: we now have a standing agenda item on the prisoner council to cover family issues and visits.

The visitor survey has been completed by PACT.

You said, we did

Following your feedback we have:

Made ice creams available for free on family days.

Made sweet bags available for families to purchase, for their loved ones to take back to house blocks.

Arranged for peer support workers who are on the Release on Temporary Licence scheme to open our centre early and to provide information and insight those with Lived Experience.

Increased the budget for free food and free entertainment on family days.

Refurbished the visits centre and conservatory.

We fund additional phone credit for those who do not receive visits.

provided more entertainment facilities for use by older children visiting the prison

How we will measure our success

Prisoner council meeting.

Reducing reoffending meeting.

Prisoner family needs questionnaire.

Prisoner Measuring the Quality of Prison Life framework and process.

Visitors family forum.

Quickly responding to and resolving complaints.

Staffing structure

Overall oversight of FaSO - The Governor

FaSO lead - strategy overseen by the Head of Reducing Reoffending

Care Experienced Lead - Offender Management Unit

Visits hall and Staffing - Head of Operations

FaSO Champion and operational Custodial Manager
